metadata.title: Night Yard, Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: a game design document in, a playable Godot project out. The prompt is a reconstruction. This game was a Unity platformer with scripts and art but no levels, rebuilt in Godot with six.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a 2.5D brawler-platformer — a night shift in a container yard, three Y Bots to choose from, ledges, wall jumps, an axe and a hammer, and a Forewoman at the end — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 6 levels, 3 Y Bots, 17 scripts, 5,215 lines.
Played here: 3 scripted-input takes, 78 of 78 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Night Yard is a side-view brawler-platformer. You climb container stacks and fight yard bots to reach the Forewoman. Every feature here is played by a script: the game's own bot brain decides, and its decisions go in as real key presses. Nobody has played it by hand yet.

props.text:
Night Yard
is a racing game.
Six levels, one boss.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. All six levels, the Forewoman, the credits, the failures and the other inputs play through real key presses, and seventy-eight assertions pass. Two defects: after Options, the pause key stops pausing, and at the character select, the arrow keys can send Enter to Back. Whether it's fair, or fun, is a person's call.
